title: Reduced relative clauses
titleVi: Rút gọn mệnh đề quan hệ
summary: Bỏ who/which/that + be để nén cả mệnh đề vào một cụm từ — dấu hiệu câu văn học thuật band 8.
whyItMatters: Ở band 7.0 bạn viết đúng mệnh đề quan hệ; ở band 8.0 bạn biết **nén** nó. Giám khảo gọi đó là *complex noun phrases*: *policies **aimed at** cutting emissions*, *households **earning** below the poverty line*. Dùng sai dạng `-ing`/`-ed` thì câu tối nghĩa ngay, nên đây là điểm ngữ pháp vừa ghi điểm vừa dễ mất điểm.

sections.heading: What reduction actually removes
body: A reduced relative clause is a relative clause with the pronoun (**who, which, that**) and the verb **be** deleted, leaving a phrase that still describes the noun: *the policy **introduced** in 2019* means *the policy **that was introduced** in 2019*.

Academic English prefers this compression because it keeps the noun phrase tight and frees the main verb for your argument. *Students who are living in dormitories* becomes *students living in dormitories*: same meaning, fewer words, more published-journal rhythm.
Only two forms do most of the work: the **present participle (-ing)** when the original verb is active, and the **past participle (-ed / V3)** when it is passive.

examples.right: The report examining air quality in Hanoi was published last week.
examples.wrong: The report which examining air quality in Hanoi was published last week.
examples.note: Active verb → **-ing**; never keep *which* and drop *be* at the same time.

examples.right: Data collected by the census suggest a north–south divide.
examples.wrong: Data collecting by the census suggest a north–south divide.
examples.note: The data do not collect anything — passive meaning needs the past participle.

examples.right: Cities facing severe congestion have started to charge drivers.
examples.note: **facing** = which face — an active habit, so -ing is correct.

sections.heading: The one condition: the pronoun must be the subject
body: You can delete **who/which/that** only when it is the **subject** of the relative clause. If it is the object, the clause already has its own subject and the reduction collapses: *the book **which I bought*** cannot become *the book bought*.
The same restriction applies after prepositions. *The city **in which** she grew up* has no reduced form, because *which* is the object of **in**.
The table shows which clauses survive reduction and which must stay full.

rows: a report that examines air quality
a trend that has continued since 2010
the scheme, which was launched in 2022
pronoun is the object, not the subject

sections.heading: Active or passive: choosing -ing or -ed
body: The choice is meaning, not decoration. **-ing** presents the noun as the doer; the **past participle** presents it as the receiver. The classic pair *developing countries* / *developed countries* shows how much rides on one letter.
With transitive verbs both forms may exist and mean opposite things: *the company **employing** 200 staff* (it employs them) versus *the staff **employed** by the company* (they are employed).
Intransitive verbs normally take **-ing** only, because there is no object to receive the action: *the population **growing** fastest*, never *the population grown fastest*.

examples.right: Families living in overcrowded housing report higher rates of stress.
examples.wrong: Families lived in overcrowded housing report higher rates of stress.
examples.note: The families are the ones doing the living — active, so **living**.

examples.right: The taxes imposed on sugary drinks reduced consumption.
examples.wrong: The taxes imposing on sugary drinks reduced consumption.
examples.note: Taxes are imposed by the government — passive.

examples.right: A government attempting to cut spending must explain its priorities.
examples.note: **attempting** = which attempts; the government is the agent.

sections.heading: Related pattern: first, only, superlative + to-infinitive
body: When the noun is **the first, the last, the only, the next** or a superlative, the relative clause often reduces to a **to-infinitive**: *She was the first researcher **to question** the official figures* (= who questioned them).

This pattern works only when the noun is the **subject** of the verb. *The first report **that the committee published*** cannot become *the first report to publish*, because the report does not publish anything.
Used sparingly, it gives a formal, evaluative tone that suits conclusions and topic sentences.

examples.right: Norway was the first country to tax carbon emissions at scale.
This is the only study to compare all five regions.
The first policy that the ministry approved was a subsidy for solar panels.
examples.wrong: The first policy to approve was a subsidy for solar panels.
examples.note: Here *policy* is the object of *approve*, so keep the full clause.

sections.heading: Where reduction earns marks in IELTS
body: In Task 2, reduced clauses let you define a group inside a noun phrase and keep the finite verb for your claim: *Policies **aimed at reducing car use** often penalise the poorest commuters.*
In Task 1, they attach data to its category economically: *Households **earning above £50,000** spent proportionally more on transport.*
Do not stack reductions. One reduced clause per noun phrase is the readable limit; beyond that, restore a full relative clause or split the sentence. Dense is not the same as complex.

examples.right: Residents affected by the new flight path have demanded compensation.
examples.note: Compact subject; the main verb *have demanded* carries the argument.

examples.right: The figure for graduates entering teaching fell sharply after 2015.
examples.note: Task 1: the reduced clause identifies the category.

examples.right: Companies pioneering green technology often struggle to scale up.
examples.wrong: Companies pioneered green technology often struggle to scale up.
examples.note: Active present meaning → **-ing**, not the past participle.

commonMistakes.wrong: The survey conducting in 2022 showed a clear pattern.
commonMistakes.right: The survey conducted in 2022 showed a clear pattern.
commonMistakes.why: The survey does not conduct anything; it **was conducted**. Passive meaning always takes the past participle. Người Việt hay dịch *được tiến hành* thành `-ing` vì thấy động từ ở dạng chủ động trong tiếng Việt.

commonMistakes.wrong: Students who living in rural areas travel further.
commonMistakes.right: Students living in rural areas travel further.
commonMistakes.why: Rút gọn là **bỏ** đại từ quan hệ, không phải giữ nó rồi bỏ *be*. Chỉ có một trong hai: *who live* hoặc *living*.

commonMistakes.wrong: The number of cars using in the city centre has fallen.
commonMistakes.right: The number of cars used in the city centre has fallen.
commonMistakes.why: Cars are used, not using. Nếu danh từ là **đối tượng** của hành động thì phải dùng V3.

commonMistakes.wrong: The data was collected from 200 students attended the university.
commonMistakes.right: The data was collected from 200 students attending the university.
commonMistakes.why: Hai động từ chia (was collected, attended) mà không có liên từ là lỗi câu. Câu thứ hai phải thành cụm rút gọn hoặc mệnh đề quan hệ đầy đủ.

commonMistakes.wrong: The first policy to approve was a subsidy for solar panels.
commonMistakes.right: The first policy that the ministry approved was a subsidy for solar panels.
commonMistakes.why: `the first + to-infinitive` chỉ dùng khi danh từ **làm** hành động. Ở đây policy bị phê duyệt, nên phải giữ mệnh đề đầy đủ.

ieltsTips: Mở đoạn Task 2 bằng một cụm rút gọn để định nghĩa nhóm đối tượng, rồi dùng mệnh đề đầy đủ cho luận điểm: *Households **renting privately** face far less security than those **living in social housing**. This insecurity, **exacerbated by short tenancies**, discourages them from investing in their neighbourhoods.*

Trong Task 1, gắn số liệu vào đúng nhóm bằng `-ing`/`-ed` thay vì viết *which*: *Graduates **employed in the public sector** earned roughly 15% less than those **working in finance**.* Câu ngắn hơn mà vẫn chính xác.
Kiểm tra dạng rút gọn bằng một câu hỏi: danh từ **làm** hành động hay **bị** hành động? Làm → `-ing`; bị → V3. Đây là bước duy nhất giúp bạn tránh lỗi *the survey conducting*.
Đừng rút gọn mệnh đề mà đại từ quan hệ là **tân ngữ**: *the book which I bought* không thể thành *the book bought*. Nếu nghi ngờ, giữ mệnh đề đầy đủ — đúng ngữ pháp luôn hơn một câu nén sai.

exercises.question: The students ___ in rural areas often face longer commutes.
options: living
lived
who living
live
exercises.explanation: Students are the ones who live there — active meaning → **living**.

exercises.question: The report ___ by the environment ministry warns of severe water stress.
options: publishing
published
which publishing
publishes
exercises.explanation: The report is published by someone — passive → past participle **published**.

exercises.question: Which sentence cannot be reduced?
options: The workers who were dismissed last month are appealing.
The city which attracts the most tourists is Da Nang.
The book which I borrowed from the library was overdue.
The trend which has continued since 2010 worries economists.
exercises.explanation: *Which* is the **object** of *borrowed*, so the clause has its own subject (*I*) and cannot be reduced.

exercises.question: Choose the correct reduced form of: *The policies that were introduced in 2019 changed the market.*
options: The policies introducing in 2019 changed the market.
The policies introduced in 2019 changed the market.
The policies which introduced in 2019 changed the market.
The policies introduce in 2019 changed the market.
exercises.explanation: Passive relative clause → past participle, with **that were** deleted.

exercises.question: Which sentence uses the to-infinitive reduction correctly?
options: She was the first scientist to identify the virus.
She was the first scientist to the virus was identified.
The virus was the first to identify by her.
She was the first scientist identifying the virus first.
exercises.explanation: **the first + noun + to-infinitive** works when the noun is the subject of the verb — *she* identifies the virus.

exercises.question: Households ___ (earn) above the national average spend more on leisure.
The data ___ (collect) between 2010 and 2020 show a steady decline.
exercises.explanation: Data are collected by researchers → past participle **collected**.

exercises.question: The number of people ___ (work) from home has doubled since 2019.
The tax ___ (impose) on single-use plastics was unpopular with manufacturers.
exercises.explanation: The tax is imposed by the government → past participle **imposed**.

exercises.question: Norway was the first country ___ (introduce) a carbon tax at national level.
exercises.explanation: **the first country** is the subject of *introduce*, so the to-infinitive reduction is correct.
